facts.text: The museum lists wheelchair accessibility throughout its exhibition galleries and theater, and wheelchair-accessible restrooms.
quote: Wheelchair accessibility throughout the museum's exhibition galleries and theater and wheelchair accessible restrooms.

facts.text: Manual wheelchairs are lent free of charge, first come, first served.
quote: Manual wheelchair rentals free of charge, available on a first-come, first-served basis.

facts.text: From the Central Riverfront Garage under Great American Ball Park, signs for the museum lead to an elevator and stairwell up to its entrance.
quote: The parking garage underneath Great American Ball Park is called the Central Riverfront Garage, and can be accessed from the Pete Rose Way entrance (at the corner of Pete Rose Way and Broadway), the Mehring Way entrance (facing the Ohio River) and the Joe Nuxhall Way entrance (across from the Museum building). It can also be accessed on Mehring Way underneath the Moerlein Lager House.
Once inside the garage, follow the signs for the Hall of Fame and Museum to access the elevator and stairwell that leads to the Hall of Fame entrance.

facts.text: All video presentations are open-captioned. Assisted listening headsets are free at the box office.
quote: Open captioning on all video presentations throughout the museum.
The museum is equipped with an assisted listening system for the hearing impaired. Headsets are available for use free of charge at the museum's box office.

facts.text: Large-format gallery floor plans are free on request at the box office.
quote: Large format museum gallery floor plans are available free of charge upon request at the museum's box office.

facts.text: Exhibits are on two floors; the museum suggests at least 45 to 60 minutes for a self-guided visit.
quote: The Cincinnati Reds Hall of Fame and Museum presented by Dinsmore is a 16,000 sq. ft. facility with exhibit galleries located on two floors. Please allow at least 45-60 minutes for your self-guided tour.

facts.text: For October–March, the museum lists Tuesday–Sunday hours of 10 a.m.–5 p.m., with closure on Mondays, Sundays of Bengals home games and major holidays. Its separate baseball-season schedule differs; confirm the date before traveling.
quote:
October – March
Tuesday – Sunday: 10:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Closed on Mondays, the Sundays of Cincinnati Bengals home games, and on major holidays.
Monday, March 23 - Wednesday, September 30
Non-Game Days
10 a.m. – 5 p.m.
Game Days
Weekday Games
6:40 or 7:10 p.m. games: 10 a.m. – 8 p.m.
Afternoon games: 10 a.m. until two hours after the game ends
Weekend Games (Saturday & Sunday)
6:40 or 7:10 p.m. games: 10 a.m. – 8 p.m.
Afternoon games: 10 a.m. until two hours after the game ends
Member Early Entry
Saturday game days: Members may enter beginning at 9 a.m.
Hours are subject to change.

facts.text: The Central Riverfront Garage's Joe Nuxhall Way entrance is across from the museum building.
quote: The parking garage underneath Great American Ball Park is called the Central Riverfront Garage, and can be accessed from the Pete Rose Way entrance (at the corner of Pete Rose Way and Broadway), the Mehring Way entrance (facing the Ohio River) and the Joe Nuxhall Way entrance (across from the Museum building). It can also be accessed on Mehring Way underneath the Moerlein Lager House.

facts.text: For ballpark tours, backpacks are prohibited except for medical or infant-care purposes; permitted bags must be no larger than 16 × 16 × 8 inches. The Hall of Fame cannot store bags, strollers or other personal possessions for guests.
quote: BACKPACKS ARE NOT PERMITTED (excluding for medical and infant care purposes). Backpacks are defined as multi-pocketed bags that are worn on the back.
All of the above must not exceed the size of 16”x16”x8”.
ALL OTHER BAGS ARE PROHIBITED. THE REDS HALL OF FAME CANNOT STORE BAGS, STROLLERS OR PERSONAL POSSESSIONS OF ANY KIND FOR GUESTS.

facts.text: The museum’s Museums for All offer gives complimentary general admission for up to four people per SNAP EBT card with valid photo ID. It excludes ballpark tours and collectible gifts.
quote: The Reds Hall of Fame and Museum presented by Dinsmore is excited to participate in the Museums for All program. Through this program, individuals and families presenting a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card and a valid form of photo ID are eligible for complimentary general admission to the museum. Up to four individuals can take of this offer per EBT card.
This offer is valid on general admission and does not apply to Great American Ball Park tours. Collectible gifts are not included with Museums for All admission.

facts.text: The museum describes its VIP Major League Clubhouse Tour as two hours long and available only in the off-season. The stated stops include dugouts, batting tunnels and clubhouses; the page does not describe step-free alternatives, rest stops or how to arrange a modified route. Confirm those needs before booking.
quote: The two-hour VIP Major League Clubhouse Tours are an expanded version of our standard ballpark tour that is ONLY available in the off season. This tour makes all of our standard stops such as the First Star Fan Zone, the Champions Club, the Handlebar, the Seating Bowl, the Warning Track, and the Dugouts, but also offers stops in areas only available in the off-season, which includes:
Reds Batting Tunnels
The Visitors Clubhouse
The Reds Clubhouse

facts.text: The standard Great American Ball Park Tour checks in at the museum lobby, covers about three-quarters of a mile and lasts about 75–90 minutes, with exposure to the weather. The Reds describe it as wheelchair- and stroller-accessible and offer complimentary wheelchairs for guests who have difficulty walking. Confirm a specific route, transfer needs and rest opportunities before booking.
quote: Guests check in for tours located in the lobby of the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum.
This is a walking tour (approximately 3/4 mile) that is subject to the elements, so we suggest wearing comfortable footwear and weather-appropriate attire.
Tours last approximately 75-90 minutes
Tours are wheelchair and stroller accessible. The Reds Hall of Fame provides complimentary wheelchairs for guests who may have difficulty walking.

facts.text: For the standard ballpark tour, all ticket sales are final and non-refundable. The itinerary can change without notice and some locations may be closed on a given tour; do not assume a particular stop will be included.
quote: Please note that the tour itinerary and locations are subject to change without notice. All locations may not be open for every tour.
All ticket sales are final and non-refundable.

facts.text: ADA seating is in Sections 101–113, 115–117, 125–127 and 131–132, and in premium Sections 333, 334, 337 and 344; a seating map is linked from the page.
quote: ADA seating is available across Nippert Stadium, in Sections 101-113, 115-117, 125-127, 131-132 and Premium Sections 333, 334, 337, and 344.
View ADA Seating Map Here (PDF)

facts.text: UC lists Woodside Garage parking at $25, by credit/debit card only, with a state-issued disability pass required and a shuttle to a drop-off near Nippert. This accessibility page does not describe Eden Garage; separate football-guide notes below cover its bus service.
quote: Parking for patrons needing accessible parking is available in Woodside Garage for a rate of $25 (credit/debit card only).
A state-issued handicap pass is required.
A shuttle from Woodside Garage to a drop off point near the stadium will be provided.

facts.text: UC describes all Nippert restrooms as ADA accessible and equipped with baby-changing stations. This is the publisher’s description; adult-changing equipment, stall dimensions and current conditions are not established.
quote: Restrooms are available throughout Nippert Stadium. All restrooms are equipped with baby changing stations and are ADA accessible.

facts.text: UC’s football guide lists open captions on prerecorded main-board videos and live captions on smartphones during games. Students, employees and visitors who are d/Deaf or hard of hearing can request ASL interpreters for UC events through its online ASL/CART form.
quote: UC offers captioning at multiple live sporting events and venues including football, men's and women's basketball, and volleyball; open captions on all pre-corded videos on the main video board; and the opportunity to access live captioning on smart phones (which can be accessed at Nippert Streamtext link during games).

Additionally, any student, employee or visitor who is d/Deaf or hard of hearing can request ASL Interpreters for any UC event, including athletics events, using our online request form: ASL/CART request . Visitors who need other access or disability-related accommodations can email our accessibility office at AccessResources@uc.edu and we will work together with campus partners to coordinate access.

facts.text: The accessible-parking shuttle from Woodside Garage to the drop-off near the stadium is a golf cart.
quote: Parking for patrons needing accessible parking is available in Woodside Garage for a rate of $25 (credit/debit card only). A golf cart shuttle from Woodside Garage to a drop off point near the stadium will be provided. A state-issued handicap pass is required. For more information, call (513) 556-2283.

facts.text: Medical bags and items must be inspected and are marked with a wristband or sticker.
quote: ALL INDIVIDUALS AND THEIR BELONGINGS ARE SUBJECT TO SEARCH. THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE WITHOUT NOTICE. Fans with medical bags or items they must carry with them must be inspected and either have a wristband or sticker placed on it to show that it has been inspected. PLEASE ARRIVE EARLIER TO AVOID LAST MINUTE GATE PRESSURE.

facts.text: There is no re-entry; in an emergency, contact the ticket taker or security supervisor at the nearest gate. UC Health staffs First Aid rooms behind sections 117 and 111, in Victory Plaza and on the West Pavilion Club level.
quote: Re-entry is not permitted at any Nippert Stadium event. In case of emergency, guests can contact the ticket taker and/or security supervisor at the nearest gate.
First Aid rooms are staffed by trained medical personnel provided by UC Health. Locations are behind sections 117, 111 and in Victory Plaza as well as in the Club level in the West Pavilion.

facts.text: For non-emergency help during a game, text (513) 450-8556. Other disability-related accommodations can be requested at AccessResources@uc.edu.
quote: For non-emergency help on gameday, fans can text (513) 450-8556 for assistance.

Additionally, any student, employee or visitor who is d/Deaf or hard of hearing can request ASL Interpreters for any UC event, including athletics events, using our online request form: ASL/CART request . Visitors who need other access or disability-related accommodations can email our accessibility office at AccessResources@uc.edu and we will work together with campus partners to coordinate access.

facts.text: Seat cushions up to 18 inches are allowed, and free lockers outside Gates B and J hold items that can't come inside.
quote: Seat cushions (no larger than 18 inches)
Lockers are available free of charge outside of Gate B and Gate J, perfect for storing items that cannot be brought into the stadium on gameday.

facts.text: Service dogs are allowed; emotional support, comfort and companion animals are not.
quote: Service animals are permitted in Nippert Stadium.
A service animal is a dog that is individually trained to perform work or tasks for a person with a disability.
Emotional support, comfort, and companion animals are not considered service animals under this policy and are not permitted in the stadium.

facts.text: For single-game football parking, the guide says some Woodside passes are pre-sold as accessible parking for $25. Bring that pass plus a state-issued disability placard or plate; the pass alone is insufficient. Golf carts run from outside the garage to an entry gate. Boarding, wheelchair carriage and transfer assistance are not described.
quote: A portion of pre-sold parking in Woodside Garage will be designated as accessible parking passes for patrons with mobility issues at a rate of $25. A state-issued handicap placard or license plate will be required on Gameday with that parking pass. Anyone showing an ADA pass without a proper placard or license plate will not be permitted to park. Golf cart shuttles will run from outside the garage to the entry gate.

facts.text: The football guide lists Eden Garage gameday parking at $25 by credit/debit card and describes its bus shuttles as ADA accessible. The listed campus drop-off is Commons Way at Daniels Street. Vehicle dimensions and the complete onward route have not been verified.
quote: Gameday parking (credit/debit card only) will be available in Eden Garage for $25. Bus shuttles from Eden Garage will be ADA accessible. For more information, call (513) 556-2283.

Bus shuttles are available from Eden Garage before, during and after the game. Shuttles start 4 hours before the game starts and will continue for one hour post-game. Shuttles will drop off at the corner of Commons Way and Daniels Street. To enter Nippert Stadium, fans can walk through Sigma Sigma Commons to enter gate J, use the sidewalk to head to Fifth Third Arena and enter into Gate A or use the sidewalk to walk around the UC Baseball Stadium and down Corry Street to enter gate B.

facts.text: Eden shuttle start times conflict within the football guide: one paragraph says seven hours before the game, another four hours. Both end one hour after the game. Confirm the departure time before planning an early arrival.
quote: Shuttle buses will be running from Eden Garage to campus starting 7 hours prior to the game until 1-hour post end of the game.

Bus shuttles are available from Eden Garage before, during and after the game. Shuttles start 4 hours before the game starts and will continue for one hour post-game. Shuttles will drop off at the corner of Commons Way and Daniels Street. To enter Nippert Stadium, fans can walk through Sigma Sigma Commons to enter gate J, use the sidewalk to head to Fifth Third Arena and enter into Gate A or use the sidewalk to walk around the UC Baseball Stadium and down Corry Street to enter gate B.

facts.text: The football guide recommends Gates A or B for east-side seats and G, H or J for west-side seats. Students with an ADA student-section ticket may enter any gate rather than being required to use Gate D. These gate recommendations do not establish a continuous step-free route to a seat.
quote: Fans who are sitting on the east side of the stadium are recommended to enter through Gates A or B. Fans who are sitting on the west side of the stadium are recommended to enter through gates G, H or J. Students who acquired a ADA ticket about the student section can enter any gate and does not need to enter through gate D. Students can also reach out to the Ticket Office for additional support on entry or can get a Fast Pass wristband and enter through any gate on gameday.

facts.text: UC’s accessibility page says live closed captions appear on each Nippert ribbon board, with live smartphone captions during every home game.
quote: Fans can now view live closed captions on each ribbon board inside Nippert Stadium. In addition, live closed-captioning will be available on your smartphone during every home game. Please visit this link to view closed-captioning on your smartphone.

facts.text: The football guide permits up to two unopened water bottles and prohibits other food or beverages. Its clear-bag policy allows medically necessary items after inspection; confirm arrangements for essential food or supplies before attending.
quote: Fans are permitted to bring up to two unopened water bottles into the stadium.
Food or Beverages (excluding the two unopened water bottles)
Exceptions to this policy will be made for all medically necessary items after proper inspection.

facts.text: Football FastPass wristbands are obtained by scanning tickets before gates open at the Fifth Third Arena ticket office, outside Tangeman University Center or at The Grid. The guide says guests obtaining FastPass cannot carry bags, so confirm how a medical bag affects this option.
quote: Fans are encouraged to utilize the FastPass and to download digital tickets to make entry as smooth as possible on gameday. Fans are able to scan their tickets prior to gates opening at the Fifth Third Arena ticket office, outside TUC, or The Grid to obtain a wristband for fast entry at one of the designated gates. To obtain a FastPass, fans are not permitted to carry bags. FastPass gates are marked on the Nippert Stadium Gates Maps.

facts.text: Nippert’s football guide lists lactation rooms in Tangeman University Center 432, Fifth Third Arena 432 behind section 108, and Lindner Athletic Center 338. Confirm which nearby building and room is available during the event; the guide does not describe a complete route from each stadium section.
quote:
Stadium lactation rooms:
Tangeman University Center, Room 432
Fifth Third Arena, Room 432 (Behind section 108)
Lindner Athletic Center, Room 338

facts.text: For football tailgating, the guide lists lactation rooms 0012A–D and 0012 in Lindner Hall’s College of Business. From its main lobby, take the elevator to floor 00 and follow the hallway to the right. Building hours and the complete route from parking are not specified.
quote: Lindner Hall - College of Business, Rooms 0012A, 0012B, 0012C, 0012D, 0012 Enter in the main lobby of the Lindner Hall/College of Business. If you take the steps down, take the first right and follow the hallway to the left of the elevators. If you take the elevator, go to floor 00. Once you are off the elevator, follow the hallway to the right.

facts.text: The university policy linked by UC athletics allows service animals with visitor handlers in campus public-accommodation areas, subject to its stated exceptions. Contact with Accessibility Resources before visiting is encouraged, not required; the policy says service animals need no identifying vest or university certification/registration.
quote: Visitors. Service Animals accompanied by a visitor Handler may be brought into areas of public accommodation on campus, unless otherwise prohibited by this Policy

While not required, Handlers are encouraged to partner with Accessibility Resources (for students and visitors) or Human Resources (for employees) before bringing a Service Animal into University facilities of public accommodation

Service Animals are not required to:
Wear a vest or other identification that indicates they are a Service Animal.
Handlers may consider having the animal wear some type of commonly recognized identification symbol identifying the animal as a Service Animal, while not disclosing the disability.
Be certified by or registered with the University.
Employee and student Handlers may consider obtaining a free University ID Card for their Service Animal by contacting Accessibility Resources (students) or Human Resources (employees).

facts.text: UC’s linked animal policy places animal care and welfare with the handler. Handlers unable to collect and dispose of waste must arrange assistance themselves, and should have a local emergency contact able to care for the animal off campus if the handler becomes unable to do so. No venue-provided animal-care service is established.
quote: The cost of care, arrangements, and responsibilities for the well-being of an animal are the sole responsibility of the Handler.

Handlers are required to clean up after and properly dispose of a Service Animal or Emotional Support Animal’s waste in a safe and sanitary manner in outdoor trash receptacles. Handlers who are not physically able to pick up and dispose of animal waste are responsible for making all necessary arrangements for assistance.

Handlers should ensure that their Service Animal or Emotional Support Animal has a care plan in place (a local emergency contact) in the event of an emergency where the Handler may be incapacitated or otherwise unable to care for the animal.
The local emergency contact must be able to care for the animal off University property while the Handler is incapacitated or otherwise unable to care for the animal.

facts.text: The basketball guide lists Campus Green and Woodside garages, University Garage Level 1 for men’s basketball, and Corry Garage for women’s basketball for disability parking with a state-issued pass. It calls this “cash parking,” but also says campus is cashless and men’s parking takes credit cards. Confirm payment and garage arrangements with the ticket office (513-556-2283).
quote: Patrons with disabilities should contact the UC Athletics Ticket Office to ensure their needs may be attended to effectively. Cash parking for patrons needing accessible parking is available in Campus Green Garage, Woodside Garage, and University Garage Level 1 (men's basketball only) and Corry Garage (women's basketball only). A state-issued handicap pass is required. For more information, call (513) 556-2283.
$10 credit card parking begins 4 hours before game time
Note: All of campus, including Fifth Third Arena, is entirely cashless.

facts.text: Pre-recorded videos on the main board have open captions, and live captioning is available on your phone during games. ASL interpreters can be requested for any UC event.
quote: UC offers captioning at multiple live sporting events and venues including football, men's and women's basketball, and volleyball; open captions on all pre-corded videos on the main video board; and the opportunity to access live captioning on smart phones (which can be accessed at Fifth Third Streamtext link during games).

Additionally, any student, employee or visitor who is d/Deaf or hard of hearing can request ASL Interpreters for any UC event, including athletics events, using our online request form: ASL/CART request. Visitors who need other access or disability-related accommodations can email our accessibility office at AccessResources@uc.edu and we will work together with campus partners to coordinate access.

facts.text: The arena follows the University of Cincinnati's service animal and emotional support animal policy.
quote: Fifth Third Arena follows the University of Cincinnati's Service Animal and Emotional Support Animal Policy, which can be viewed HERE .

facts.text: UC asks fans with disabilities to contact the Athletics Ticket Office (513-556-2283) about their needs. Other disability-related accommodations can be requested at AccessResources@uc.edu, where the accessibility office coordinates with campus partners.
quote: Patrons with disabilities should contact the UC Athletics Ticket Office to ensure their needs may be attended to effectively. Cash parking for patrons needing accessible parking is available in Campus Green Garage, Woodside Garage, and University Garage Level 1 (men's basketball only) and Corry Garage (women's basketball only). facts.text: The clear-bag policy makes exceptions for medically necessary items after inspection.
quote: Exceptions to this policy will be made for all medically necessary items after proper inspection.

facts.text: There is no re-entry at Fifth Third Arena.
quote: There is no re-entry at Fifth Third Arena.

facts.text: The first-aid center is on the north side of the main-level concourse by the Armory Bar; a nursing suite is on the same concourse behind section 109.
quote: Emergency medical personnel are on duty at each athletics event. Medical personnel can be contacted during an event by notifying the nearest event staff member, usher, or security guard and informing them of the situation and location of the incident. The first-aid center is located on the north side of the arena on the main-level concourse by the Armory Bar.
A nursing suite is located on the main-level concourse on the north side behind section 109.

facts.text: The basketball guide places restrooms mainly at the corners of both the main and upper concourses. It does not specify stall layouts, adult-changing equipment or a route from each seating area.
quote: Restrooms are located throughout the arena, typically on the corners of both the main-level and upper-level concourses.

facts.text: For men’s basketball, the guide lists shuttles between Campus Green and Dabney Circle, and University Circle and Dabney Circle, starting two hours before the game and continuing one hour afterward. It does not describe boarding equipment, wheelchair carriage or transfer assistance.
quote: Shuttles will run between Campus Green and Dabney Circle, and between University Circle and Dabney Circle, beginning two hours before game time and one hour after the game.

facts.text: For questions during basketball events, the Fan First Center is on the east concourse. Event staff, ushers or security can contact medical personnel; the First Aid center is by the Armory Bar on the north main concourse.
quote: Have a question? Want a roster card? Need a poster? The Fan First Center is the place to go! Located on the east concourse, it's the go-to area for schedule cards, posters, roster cards and more! There are also First Game Certificates and Happy Birthday Certificates available for fans!

Emergency medical personnel are on duty at each athletics event. Medical personnel can be contacted during an event by notifying the nearest event staff member, usher, or security guard and informing them of the situation and location of the incident. The first-aid center is located on the north side of the arena on the main-level concourse by the Armory Bar.

facts.text: The basketball guide lists rental lockers outside the arena’s northwest side at Lindner Athletic Building for items that cannot be brought inside. It does not give a fee, locker dimensions or a medical-equipment storage arrangement.
quote: Lockers are available for rent outside of Fifth Third Arena on the northwest side, (Lindner Athletic Building), perfect for storing items that cannot be brought into the stadium on gameday.

facts.text: For UC commencement specifically, the university directs guests needing access assistance to the far-left East Concourse doors when facing the arena, at the Oscar Robertson statue. Staff inside help with seating and accommodations. Confirm the ceremony’s arrangements; these directions are not the basketball entrance policy.
quote: Guests with accessibility needs should enter the venue at the following location:
Fifth Third Arena - East Concourse, doors to the far left when looking at arena. East Concourse is the entrance at the Oscar Robertson basketball statue.
Once inside the venue, staff will be available to offer guidance on accessible seating and accommodations.

facts.text: For UC commencement, passenger drop-off is reached by entering Woodside Drive from Martin Luther King Drive; golf carts take guests with access needs to the ceremony entrance. Guests may bring their own wheelchairs. The page does not establish cart boarding or wheelchair carriage.
quote: For guests with accessibility needs, passenger drop-off is available by entering Woodside Drive from Martin Luther King Drive. Golf carts will shuttle guests with accessibility needs from the drop-off point to the accessibility entrance of the ceremony venue.
Guests are welcome to bring their own wheelchair to the venue if needed.

facts.text: UC’s commencement guest page says ASL interpretation and live captioning are provided during the ceremony. This statement applies to commencement.
quote: ASL interpreting and live captioning are provided during the ceremony.

facts.text: For UC commencement, a free parking pass is required and accessible spaces in all parking facilities are first come, first served. Graduates receive instructions for obtaining the pass; a valid UC parking permit may also be used. This does not establish free event parking for basketball.
quote: A free pass will be required to park on the day of the ceremony. Graduates will be emailed information on securing a free parking pass for Commencement.
Accessible parking is available in all parking facilities on a first come, first served basis.
Valid parking permit holders may utilize their UC parking permit.

facts.text: UC’s single-occupancy restroom list names Shoemaker Center/Fifth Third Arena rooms 109, 323, 372, 411, 420B, 451, 486A, 4M51, 514, 588 and 686B. The list does not establish which are open to event guests, door/stall features or adult-changing equipment; ask staff for the appropriate room.
quote: A list of single occupancy restrooms around campus is maintained by the Office of Planning, Design & Construction.

facts.text: NKU says all performance venues have accessible seating; a house manager or usher can help. Guests who need special seating because of a medical condition should contact the box office at least 48 hours ahead; availability depends on the performance venue.
quote: All performance venues have handicap accessible seating . Please see a House Manager or Usher for assistance.

Guests requiring special seating consideration due to a medical condition should contact the Box Office to make advance arrangements with a minimum of 48 hours notice. Availability depends on the performance venue.

facts.text: Corbett Theatre performances have reserved seats; Stauss Theatre and Greaves Concert Hall are general seating. Venues open about 30 minutes before curtain, and Stauss Theatre has no late seating.
quote: Corbett Theatre performances are reserved seating .
Stauss Theatre and Greaves Concert Hall performances are general seating .
Venues will open for seating approximately 30 minutes prior to curtain.

facts.text: If you don't have a phone or printer for your tickets, box office staff can check you in.
quote: If guests do not have a mobile device or home printing capabilities, tickets can be checked in by box office staff.

facts.text: Lots D and I are designated for SOTA events including music concerts, theatre/dance productions and gallery receptions. For student recitals, Henry Theatre productions and general gallery visits, the event policy instead directs visitors to the Welcome Center Garage. No food or drink is permitted in Fine Arts Center performance venues.
quote: Parking Lots D and I have been designated for NKU SOTA events, including music concerts, theatre & dance productions, and art gallery receptions.
If attending student recitals, productions in The Henry Theatre, or general art gallery visits, guests should use the Welcome Center Garage .
No food or drinks are permitted in any performance venue in the Fine Arts Center.

facts.text: The Fine Arts Center has an adjacent cul-de-sac for drop-off and pick-up only, with no parking. The SOTA directions list a fee for Welcome Center Garage parking for student recitals/productions and general gallery visits. Curb transitions and the complete route from vehicle to entrance are not described.
quote: There is a cul-de-sac next to the Fine Arts Center available for drop-off and pick-up only . No parking.
Parking is available for a fee in the Welcome Center Garage for student recitals/productions and general gallery visits.

facts.text: NKU directs visitors into the Fine Arts Center through the row of glass doors, with Greaves Concert Hall immediately inside. For Corbett’s accessible entrance, turn right from Greaves lobby, go through the double doors, then look ahead and slightly right for another set of doors with ADA signs. Early arrivals should wait there for an usher; box-seat holders are directed to the second-floor entrance instead.
quote: Enter the Fine Arts Center at the row of glass doors; immediately inside these doors is Greaves Concert Hall.

Corbett Theatre Accessible Entrance
From Greaves lobby, turn Right and go straight until you pass through a set of double doors.
Ahead and slightly to the right you will see another set of double doors with ADA signs directing you to Corbett Theatre
If you arrive early, please wait here for an usher to assist you to your seats once the theatre is open for seating.
If you have Box Seats, please follow the above directions to the second floor for entry at the top of the theatre.

facts.text: For the Corbett Theatre upper entrance and box office, turn right from Greaves lobby and pass through the double doors; turn left to the elevator immediately on the left. Take it to floor 2, turn right, and continue to the hallway end; Corbett, the Community Showcase Atrium and box office are on the left. This is the upper entrance, not the separate signed accessible-seating entrance.
quote:

facts.text: The SOTA box office is cashless and accepts credit cards only: Visa, MasterCard and Discover. American Express is not accepted. Arrange an accepted payment method before travel.
quote:
Transactions are now cashless.

facts.text: SOTA lists live box-office assistance Tuesday and Thursday, noon–4 p.m., and physical opening one hour before ticketed events. Outside live hours, callers can leave voicemail at 859-572-5464 or email boxoffice@nku.edu; no callback time is promised.
quote: For phone orders or inquiries, please leave a voicemail at (859) 572-5464 and your call will be returned as soon as possible. Or email boxoffice@nku.edu with any other questions.

For live assistance , please visit or contact the box office during the following hours:
Tuesday Noon - 4 p.m.
Thursday Noon - 4 p.m.
The physical box office will also open one hour before ticketed events for any night of show needs.

facts.text: If NKU closes for inclement weather, scheduled performances that day are canceled. Guests may receive a refund or exchange to another date of the same production, subject to availability; the box office says it will contact guests and make every effort to announce cancellations through its voicemail, website and local media.
quote:
If NKU closes due to inclement weather conditions, all scheduled performances on that day will be canceled.
If a performance is canceled, guests may receive a refund or exchange for another date of the same production, subject to availability.
Box office staff will call guests to make arrangements, or guests may also call the box office.
The box office will make every effort to alert guests in advance on its voice mail message, website, and local media if a performance is canceled.

facts.text: NKU’s general visitor policy requires both a valid state-issued disability placard and a Parking Services permit for its designated disability spaces. It directs visitors to the Nunn Drive office Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–4:30 p.m. or Friday 8 a.m.–4 p.m., with summer hours subject to change. Special-event arrangements are coordinated with Parking Services; confirm the SOTA event’s permit and after-hours procedure at 859-572-5505.
quote: Handicap spaces are available to visitors with ADA needs. These spaces require a valid state issued handicap placard and a permit issued by Parking Services. Please stop by the Parking Services on Nunn Drive between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. to obtain a permit Monday-Thursday or 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. on Friday (summer hours may vary).

All requests to accommodate visitors for special events need to be coordinated with Parking Services, via the submission of a special parking request form which is located on our website. If you have specific visitor parking questions please call us at (859) 572-5505.

facts.text: The general visitor-parking page names Arena, University and Kenton garages and tells drivers to pull a ticket even when entry gates are raised. It lists Visa, MasterCard and Discover, a $12 lost-ticket day rate, and possible departmental validation. Confirm the event’s garage and validation arrangements before returning to the vehicle.
quote: Visitor parking is located in the Arena Garage, University Garage, and Kenton Garages (Interactive Campus Map) . Always pull a ticket as you enter the garage, even if the gates are up. If you do not pull a ticket you must press the lost ticket button and pay the maximum day rate of $12.00 . Garages accept Visa, MasterCard, and Discover . If you cannot provide proper payment at exit you will receive a $24.00 non-payment of garage fees citation. Some departments validate parking, be sure to check with department prior to heading back to vehicle.

facts.text: The Redden Gardens fridge is listed on Doc John Redden Way at 909 Scott Boulevard. COVUnity describes its Covington fridges as free, open every day around the clock, and self-serve with no staff present.
quote: Two free spots in Covington, open day and night. Anyone can donate or take. Swing by whenever it suits you. There is no staff present and no schedule to keep because it is self-serve.
Open 24/7 · every day of the year
Doc John Redden Way 909 Scott Blvd Covington, KY 41011

facts.text: COVUnity says anyone may take food without signing in or explaining their need. No sign-up, cost or questions are required; the site does not establish assisted shopping or delivery.
quote: The COVUnity Fridge is Covington's free community fridge and pantry. Two locations, stocked by neighbors and open around the clock. If you need food, it's yours. No sign-up, no questions.
Hungry, stretched thin, or just passing by? Help yourself. It's free and open to everyone, and nobody's going to ask you to sign in or explain why you're there.

facts.text: The operator lists refrigerated and frozen food, a microwave and a hot/cold water station at Redden Gardens. These are published amenities, not confirmation that equipment is working or stocked at the time of a visit.
quote: The main fridge, with refrigerated and frozen food, a microwave, and a hot & cold water station.

facts.text: The operator asks visitors to shut the fridge door tightly, wipe spills and discard items past their prime. Donations must exclude opened or expired food and unlabeled prepared or home-cooked food; labeled meals from commercial kitchens are accepted. Individual food suitability is not established.
quote: Wipe up spills, toss anything past its prime, and shut the door tight. A few seconds of care keeps the next person's food safe and the fridge worth coming back to.
Labeled meals from a commercial kitchen
Opened or expired food
Unlabeled prepared or home-cooked food

facts.text: A free NKY Health wellness kiosk is described immediately to the left of the main Redden Gardens fridge, open around the clock without sign-up. Supplies may vary. The source does not describe the approach, door controls or reach to its compartments.

facts.text: COVUnity describes the fridge as supplemental food support and directs people needing recurring help to established social services. It says it has no staff and relies on community helpers, so prompt personal assistance is not assured.
quote: We recognize we are not solving hunger alone. We rely on established social services to help meet ongoing need, and we are supplemental to these resources.

If you are in need of recurring help, please reach out to these services. Be Concerned, for example, offers monthly pantry registration, emergency food assistance, mobile pantry support, and homebound delivery. The direct links below can take you straight to local pantries, churches, and assistance programs.

Send us a message with an open question. Want to pitch in, drop off a donation, ask about an item request, or find out about starting a fridge where you live? We do not have staff, so we rely on helpers in the community, but we'll get back to you when we can.
